> 🛑 **PROBE WATCHDOG — MANDATORY (added 2026-05-31)**: Run EVERY probe through the wall-clock watchdog — `node scripts/run-probe.mjs --max-time 180 TI-84_Plus_CE/probe-X.mjs` in the FOREGROUND with the Bash tool `timeout: 300000`. **NEVER** run `node <probe>` bare and **NEVER** use `run_in_background` for a probe. Root cause of the 2026-05-31 incident: a lifted block can infinite-loop *inside a single `cpu.step()`*, so the probe's own `maxSteps` never fires; the Bash-tool timeout does not cascade to the child on Windows; and a backgrounded probe escapes the tool timeout entirely. Result was probe-phase482-decode-cursor-render.mjs orphaned at ~6h / 21,800s CPU and the auto-loop hung. The watchdog spawns the probe as a child and tree-kills it at the cap (exit 124) from a parent whose event loop is free — the only enforced cap. Keep `--max-time` strictly below the Bash tool `timeout` so the watchdog reaps the child first. Golden regression takes ~14s, so 180s is generous.

  - `CALL 0x08C308` — BPP flag test (BIT 2,D000C6)

(2) ★★★★ 0x0A26D6 RENDERER EARLY EXIT + STRING OUTPUT (probe-phase552-decode-0A26D6.mjs, Sonnet+Opus-verified):

- **Sequence**: POP HL, EXX, POP BC/DE/HL (restore shadow regs), EXX, POP AF (restore interrupt state), JP PO,0x0A26E2 (skip EI if interrupts were disabled), EI, POP BC, SCF, RET.

(3) ★★★★ 0x07BF3E GLYPH TABLE LOOKUP DECODED (probe-phase552-decode-07BF3E.mjs, Sonnet+Opus-verified):
- **0x07BF3E (76B, 0x07BF3E-0x07BF8A)**: Glyph data copier.

- **Main path (0x07BF5C)**:
  1. EX DE,HL → DE = 28 × char_code (the offset)
  2. CALL 0x000380 → returns HL = font table base address
  3. ADD HL,DE → HL = font_base + 28 × char_code (pointer to glyph data)
  4. LD DE,0x000000; LD (D005A1),DE; LD (D005A3),DE → clears 6 bytes at D005A1-D005A6 (glyph metadata header)
  5. LD DE,0xD005A5; LD BC,0x001C; LDIR → copies 28 bytes from HL (ROM glyph data) to D005A5-D005C0
  6. LD HL,0xD005A1; LDI×4 → copies 4 bytes from D005A1 onwards (the cleared header)
  7. LD HL,0xD005A1; RET → returns HL pointing to the glyph buffer
- **KEY INSIGHT**: The glyph data lives at D005A1-D005C0 (32 bytes total: 4-byte header + 28-byte glyph bitmap). 0x000380 is the font base address provider — decoding it will reveal where the font bitmaps live in ROM.
- **D005A1-D005A4**: Cleared to 0x00 (metadata/padding). D005A5-D005C0: 28 bytes of actual glyph bitmap data.

- **0x0A24C8-0x0A26C7 (~512B)**: The complete glyph pixel rendering engine.
- **Entry setup (0x0A24C8-0x0A2536)**:
  - INC IX (advance past glyph header byte)
  - BIT 0,(IY+0x23) → if set, adds kerning offset from D0266F to IX
  - BIT 6/2,(IY+0x32) → selects column width: B=5 for special modes, else B = min(E, 8) for standard, with D = E - B (remaining pixels for next pass)
  - Loads framebuffer pointer from (D0059C), loads saved y-coord from (D005A0)
  - CALL 0x0A1A9D and CALL 0x0A1B1C → compute framebuffer row start address from x,y coordinates
  - Sets up BC, HL (framebuffer pointer), DE (color/stride state)
- **Glyph data read (0x0A253B)**: LD A,(IX+0x00), INC IX — reads one byte of glyph bitmap, advances IX. BIT 3,(IY+0x05) → if set, CPL (invert glyph for reverse video).
- **Three rendering paths (based on IY+0x4A flags)**:
  - **Path 1 — BIT 5,(IY+0x4A) set (0x0A254F-0x0A258B)**: 1-bit monochrome rendering. DJNZ loop at 0x0A2589→0x0A255F. SLA C walks through glyph bits. If bit set → writes foreground color; if clear → writes background. SRL B / LD B,0x80 handles byte boundary crossing in framebuffer. BIT 7,D controls row doubling (advance by 0x28=40 bytes between doubled rows).
  - **Path 2 — BIT 6,(IY+0x4A) set (0x0A2597-0x0A2614)**: 4-bit color/bold rendering. Similar SLA C bit-walking but with OR operations for color blending. OR 0xD0/0x0D/0xB0/0x0B applies different color intensities based on BIT 7,B and row position. RRCA×4 rotates nibbles. DJNZ at 0x0A2612→0x0A25B7. Uses BIT 1,(IY+0x14) for font size (row offset 0x85=133 for large, 0x5D=93 for small).
  - **Path 3 — default (0x0A2618-0x0A2694)**: Standard 16-bit color rendering. CALL 0x08C308 (likely color lookup). Two sub-paths based on carry: writes E/D (foreground) or C/B (background) as 16-bit pixel pairs. DJNZ loops at 0x0A2634 and 0x0A2682. LD (HL),C/LD (HL),E writes low byte, INC HL, LD (HL),B/LD (HL),D writes high byte — standard 16-bit color pixel write.
- **Row advancement (0x0A2660/0x0A26B4)**:
  - LD HL,(D0059C), LD BC,0x000140 (=320), ADD HL,BC, LD (D0059C),HL — advances framebuffer by one row (320 bytes = 160 pixels × 2 bytes for 16-bit color). Wait — 320 = 160 pixels at 16bpp. But the LCD is 320 pixels wide, which would be 640 bytes per row at 16bpp.
  - Second path uses LD BC,0x000280 (=640) — this IS the full 320-pixel row stride at 16bpp.
  - So 0x140 = half-row (used in split-screen or small font mode?), 0x280 = full row.
- **Outer loop (0x0A266F/0x0A26C3)**: DEC B, JP NZ,0x0A2537 — loops back to render next glyph row. B counts the remaining rows of the glyph (set during row height calculation at 0x0A2493-0x0A24C8).
- **Function end**: 0x0A26C7 POP HL, falls through to 0x0A26D6 (the cleanup/exit path with register restore and RET).
- **KEY ARCHITECTURE**: The full character renderer 0x0A23E5 spans 0x0A23E5-0x0A26E4 = **767 bytes**. It is the single largest function decoded in this project. The three rendering paths handle monochrome, 4-bit color, and 16-bit color respectively, selected by attribute flags in IY+0x4A.

(3) ★★★★ 0x061DEF/0x061E20 SETJMP/LONGJMP PAIR DECODED (probe-phase541-decode-061DEF.mjs, Codex+Opus-verified):
- **0x061DEF (49B, 0x061DEF-0x061E1F) — setjmp**:
  - POP DE (saves return address), PUSH HL (save caller's context pointer).
  - LD HL,(D008E0) → PUSH HL (save previous jmp_buf SP).

  - EX DE,HL → JP (HL) — **returns to caller** (DE held the return address).
- **0x061E20 (7B) — longjmp**:
  - POP BC (discard longjmp's own return address).
  - LD SP,(D008E0) — **restores SP to setjmp point**.
  - RET — pops the cleanup handler address (0x061E27) pushed by setjmp, jumps there.
- **0x061E27 (12B) — cleanup handler** (jumped to after longjmp):
  - POP AF×3 (unwind the 3 pushed context values).
  - EX (SP),HL → LD (D008E0),HL — restores previous jmp_buf SP from stack.
  - POP HL, POP AF, PUSH BC, RET — returns to the code after the setjmp CALL with BC on stack.
- **0x061E33 (12B) — error dispatch helper**:

- **0x061E3F (extended setjmp)**: Same as 0x061DEF but with PUSH DE, PUSH IX preservation — saves IX in the jmp_buf.
- **KEY RAM**: D008E0 (SP save), D0258A-D02593 (error handler chain, 4 pointers).

(2) ★★★★ 0x061DD1 RECOVERY HANDLER DECODED (probe-phase542-decode-061DD1.mjs, Codex+Sonnet, Opus-verified):
- **0x061DD1 (30B)**: Restores the error handler chain context saved by setjmp:
  - `LD HL,(D02590)` + `POP DE` + `ADD HL,DE` + `LD (D02593),HL` — restores handler chain pointer 2 (base + delta).
  - `POP DE` + `LD HL,(D0258A)` + `ADD HL,DE` + `LD (D0258D),HL` — restores handler chain pointer 1.
  - `POP HL` + `LD (D008E0),HL` — restores previous jmp_buf SP.
  - `LD A,(D008DF)` — loads error code into A.
  - `RET` — returns to original caller with error code in A.
- **PURPOSE**: This is the "unwind" path after longjmp → cleanup (0x061E27) → recovery (0x061DD1). It reverses the delta-encoded context that setjmp pushed, restoring the previous error handler frame. The delta encoding (SBC in setjmp, ADD in recovery) is a compact way to save/restore relative pointers without needing absolute copies.
- **SETJMP/LONGJMP FLOW NOW FULLY MAPPED**:
  - setjmp (0x061DEF): push prev SP + compute/push deltas for D0258A↔D0258D and D02590↔D02593 + push 0x061DD1 + push 0x061E27 + save SP to D008E0
  - longjmp (0x061E20): restore SP from D008E0, RET → 0x061E27
  - cleanup (0x061E27): pop 3 context values, restore prev jmp_buf, return
  - recovery (0x061DD1): restore chain pointers via delta-add, restore prev SP, load error code, RET
- **0x061DB2 SHARED ERROR HANDLER (31B)**: LD (D008DF),A (save error code) → CALL 0x03E1B4 (interrupt-safe wrapper) → RES 7,(IY+75) / RES 2,(IY+18) / RES 4,(IY+36) / RES 1,(IY+73) (clear 4 OS flags) → LD SP,(D008E0) → POP AF → RET (into setjmp recovery chain).

- **Entry (0x07C9AF-0x07C9B3)**: FD CB 48 5E = BIT 3,(IY+48); C0 = RET NZ. Quick exit if IY+48 bit 3 is set (already normalized).
- **Leading-zero check (0x07C9B4-0x07C9BB)**: LD HL,D005FA; LD A,(HL); AND 0xF0; JR NZ,0x07C9E1 (upper nibble present → skip to sign normalization).
- **Normalization loop (0x07C9BD-0x07C9D0)**: LD C,0x10 (max 16 shifts). Loop: DEC C; JP Z,0x07FAC2 (overflow → zero OP1). CALL 0x07FB48 (BCD shift left). INC HL; LD A,(HL); AND 0xF0; JP Z,0x07C9BF (continue shifting until upper nibble appears).
- **Exponent adjust (0x07C9D0-0x07C9E0)**: LD A,0x10; SUB C (shifts performed = 16-C). LD C,A. LD A,(D005F9); SUB C; JP C,0x07FAC2 (underflow → zero). LD (D005F9),A (store adjusted exponent). Falls through to 0x07C9E1.
- **CALL targets**: 0x07FB48. **JP targets**: 0x07FAC2 (zero OP1), 0x07C9E1 (sign normalize).
- **KEY INSIGHT**: This is the mantissa left-shift normalizer — ensures the first significant BCD digit is in the upper nibble of D005FA. The exponent is decremented by the number of shifts.

(2) ★★★★ 0x07C9E1 SIGN NORMALIZATION DECODED (probe-phase531-decode-07C9E1-sign-normalize.mjs, Codex, Opus-verified):

- **Guard byte check (0x07C9EB-0x07C9F5)**: LD HL,D00601 (OP2 guard byte). LD A,(HL); LD (HL),0x00 (read and clear guard). DEC HL (→D00600). ADD A,0xB0 (threshold check: carry if guard ≥ 0x50). RET NC (no overflow).
- **Overflow path (0x07C9F6-0x07CA01)**: CALL 0x07FBCA (BCD rounding/carry propagation). RET NC (absorbed). INC HL; LD (HL),0x10 (set mantissa MSB to 0x10 = "1.0"). JP 0x07FE1A (increment exponent).

- **KEY INSIGHT**: After BCD arithmetic, the guard byte (D00601) may contain overflow digits. This function rounds them into the mantissa. If rounding itself overflows (carry propagates through all digits), it resets mantissa to 0x10 and increments the exponent.

CP 0x80 (compare normalized result with bias). RET Z (no adjustment needed). JP 0x07FE1A (exponent increment: INC (D005F9); RET NZ; JP 0x061D02).
- **PURPOSE**: Temporarily sets OP1 exponent to 0x80 (bias midpoint), runs normalization to determine digit structure, restores original exponent, then adjusts exponent if normalization changed it. D=0x09 parameterizes the normalization depth.
- **0x0685FE (separate function, 12B)**: LD A,(D0250F); CP 0xFF; RET Z; LD D,A; JP 0x07CBB5. Loads a parameter from D0250F and calls normalization directly.

(3) ★★★★ 0x07CBB5 FP NORMALIZATION CORE DECODED (probe-phase529-decode-07CBB5-fp-normalize-core.mjs, Codex+Opus verification):
- **0x07CBB5 (~120B, 0x07CBB5-0x07CC2C)**: Multi-phase BCD mantissa normalization with rounding.
- **Phase 1 — Exponent check (0x07CBB5-0x07CBBA)**: CALL 0x07FF38 (LD A,(D005F9); CP 0x80; RET). JR NC,0x07CBDB (exp ≥ 0x80 → phase 3 skip-ahead).
- **Phase 2a — Small exponent path (0x07CBBB-0x07CBCD)**: CP 0x70 (check minimum). JR C,0x07CBD7 (exp < 0x70 → JP 0x07FAC2 reinit as zero BCD). OR 0xF0; LD L,A (round up lower nibble). LD A,D (=0x09 from caller); INC A; ADD A,L (compute offset). JP NC,0x07FAC2 (overflow → reinit). CPL; AND 0x0F; DEC A (compute shift count from complement). JR 0x07CBE3 (→ shift logic).
- **Phase 2b — OP check (0x07CBCF-0x07CBDA)**: CALL 0x07FD4A (check OP1 mantissa zero). JP NZ,0x07F7D6 (LD HL,D005F8; AND 0xC0; LD (HL),A — strip type, keep sign). JP 0x07FAC2 (zero mantissa → reinit).
- **Phase 3 — Large exponent path (0x07CBDB-0x07CBE2)**: SUB 0x80; LD L,A (remove bias). LD A,0x0D; SUB D; SUB L (compute 13 - D - unbiased_exp). RET C (negative = no normalization needed — exponent is already within range).
- **Phase 4 — Mantissa byte shift (0x07CBE3-0x07CBF1)**: SRL A (divide shift by 2 for bytes vs nibbles, carry=odd). LD HL,D00600. JR Z skip (no whole-byte shifts). LD B,A; Loop: LD A,(HL); LD (HL),0x00; DEC HL; DJNZ (shift mantissa bytes right, clearing vacated positions).
- **Phase 5 — BCD rounding (0x07CBF2-0x07CC07)**: JR NC,0x07CC02 (even shift → check full byte). Odd shift: LD A,(HL); AND 0xF0; LD (HL),A (clear lower nibble); AND 0x0F; CP 0x05; LD B,0x10 (round-up amount for upper nibble). Even shift: CP 0x50; LD B,0x01 (round-up for lower byte). JR C,0x07CBCF (digit < 5 → no round, go to OP check).
- **Phase 6 — Apply rounding (0x07CC08-0x07CC2C)**: LD A,(D005F9); PUSH AF (save exponent). LD A,(D005F8); PUSH AF (save type). XOR A; LD (D005F8),A (clear type for clean BCD add). LD A,B; CALL 0x07FBE4 (BCD add: LD B,8; JR → 8-byte ADD+ADC+DAA chain on OP1 mantissa). POP AF; AND 0x80; LD (D005F8),A (restore sign only). LD HL,D005F9; LD D,(HL) (read normalized exponent). POP AF; LD (HL),A (restore original exponent). CP D; RET Z (no exponent change). Continues if exponent changed.
- **KEY INSIGHT**: This is the core BCD normalization used by all FP operations. It handles denormalization (exp < 0x80), overflow detection, mantissa alignment by shifting bytes right, and banker's rounding (≥5 rounds up). Called from 0x0685DF (the exponent save wrapper).
- **CALL targets**: 0x07FF38, 0x07FD4A, 0x07FBE4, 0x07FAC2, 0x07F7D6.

- **Phase 1 — Setup**: CALL 0x069CBF (LD HL,D00601; XOR A; JP 0x07FA91 — clears OP2 guard byte). CALL 0x069CC8 (LD HL,D0060C; same clear for OP3 guard byte). CALL 0x07FD50 (LD A,(D00605); AND A — check OP2 exponent). JP Z,0x061D06 (zero divisor → type-code dispatch table with 8 type codes 0x82-0x9E).

- **Phase 3 — Exponent normalize**: CALL 0x080037 (LD A,(D005F9); SUB (D00604) — exponent difference). ADD A,0x80 → LD (D0060F),A (store biased exponent diff in OP3 sign byte as intermediate). CALL 0x07FB15 (RRD chain on D005FA+: shift mantissa right, BCD digit rotation). CALL 0x07FE1A (INC (D005F9) — increment OP1 exponent).
- **Phase 4 — Division loop (0x069D0B-0x069D31)**: PUSH AF (save loop counter). LD B,0x00 (quotient digit = 0). CALL 0x07FC7C (BCD 8-byte SUB+SBC+DAA chain: OP1_mantissa -= OP3_mantissa). JR C,0x069D17 (underflow → need to restore). INC B (quotient digit++). JR 0x069D0E (try again — count how many times we can subtract). 0x069D17: CALL 0x07FBFC (BCD 8-byte ADD+ADC+DAA chain: OP1_mantissa += OP3_mantissa — restore). DEC (D005F9) (decrement exponent). CALL 0x07FB48 (RLD chain on D00601: shift mantissa left). LD A,B; OR A; JR NZ → CALL 0x069D49 (store quotient digit into OP3 mantissa at computed BCD nibble position via RRA/RLA rotation). POP AF; SUB 1; JR NC,0x069D0B (loop until exponent counter exhausted).
- **Phase 5 — Epilogue (0x069D33-0x069D48)**: XOR A; LD HL,D0060C; CALL 0x07FB4C (RLD chain — final mantissa normalize). CALL 0x07C9AF (BIT 3,(IY+72); RET NZ — IY flag check). CALL 0x07FD0E (copy+swap normalize). CALL 0x07C9AF (repeat IY check). RET.
- **Sub-function 0x069D49 (quotient digit store, 36B)**: Takes A=loop counter, B=quotient digit. Reads D0060F (intermediate exponent), AND 0x0F, SUB counter. Computes byte+nibble position via RRA (halve for byte offset, carry=odd/even nibble). If even: RLA×4 to upper nibble. If odd: AND 0x0F + OR (HL) merge. Writes at D00610+offset.
- **BCD primitives**: 0x07FC7C = 8-byte BCD subtract (SUB+SBC+DAA chain, D0060C-D00601). 0x07FBFC = 8-byte BCD add (ADD+ADC+DAA chain, same buffers). 0x07FB15/0x07FB19 = RRD chain (rotate right decimal, 8 bytes). 0x07FB48/0x07FB4C = RLD chain (rotate left decimal, 8 bytes). (2) ★★★★ 0x07FE65 + 0x07FE2F TYPE TRANSFORM PAIR FULLY DECODED (Opus inline analysis, verified against ROM bytes):
- **Forward Transform (0x07FE65, 32B)**: PUSH DE/BC/HL. LD D,A (save original). AND 0x3F (strip sign bits). LD HL,0x07FE91 (input table). LD BC,5. CPIR (search for type in 5-entry table). JR NZ,0x07FE85 (not found → restore original A from D, POP and RET). Found: LD HL,0x07FE8A; ADD HL,BC (index into output table). LD B,(HL). POP HL. LD A,D; AND 0xC0 (preserve sign bits from original). OR B (merge new type). POP BC/DE. RET.
- **Reverse Transform (0x07FE2F, 32B)**: PUSH BC/HL. AND 0x3F. LD HL,0x07FE8A (output table). LD BC,6. CPIR. JR Z,found. Not found: LD B,0x0C (default=complex). JR skip. Found: LD HL,0x07FE90; ADD HL,BC; LD B,(HL). Skip: POP HL; LD A,(HL); AND 0xC0; OR B. POP BC. RET.
- **Type-code mapping tables**:
  - Input table at 0x07FE91 (5 entries): [0x0C, 0x1B, 0x1D, 0x1E, 0x1F]
  - Output table at 0x07FE8A (7 entries): [0x21, 0x20, 0x1C, 0x18, 0x00, 0x19, 0x1B]
  - **Forward mapping**: 0x0C(complex)→0x00(real), 0x1B→0x18(result), 0x1D(list)→0x1C(matrix), 0x1E→0x20, 0x1F→0x21. Not found → unchanged.
  - **Reverse mapping**: 0x21→0x1F, 0x20→0x1E, 0x1C(matrix)→0x1D(list), 0x18(result)→0x1B, 0x00(real)→0x0C(complex), 0x19→0x1B. Not found → 0x0C(complex) default.
  - **Sign preservation**: Top 2 bits (0xC0 mask) from the original type byte are preserved across both transforms.
- **PURPOSE**: These routines convert between "outer" type codes (complex/list/etc.) and "inner" type codes (real/matrix/etc.) used during FP comparison/normalization. Complex numbers (0x0C) get their real part compared as type 0x00 (real), and lists (0x1D) get compared as matrices (0x1C).

- **Frame layout**: IX-9 = OP1 save slot (9 bytes), IX-18 = OP2 save slot (9 bytes). Total frame = 18 bytes for FP register saves.

Dual VRAM path via CALL 0x08C308: (a) Non-zero → LD DE,(E30010) alternate VRAM base, row advance 0x000140 (320 bytes), 1-byte pixel writes; (b) Zero → LD DE,D40000 standard VRAM, row advance 0x000280 (640 bytes), 2-byte pixel writes (LD (HL),E + LD (HL),D). Both paths use DJNZ for pixel fill within a row, outer loop DEC A / JR NZ for rows. D0059C used as VRAM cursor (saved/restored per row).

## ★★★ Workflow Probe Mandate (READ FIRST — added 2026-05-14)

**The "plateau" risk**: ROM coverage is 95.92% and excellent infrastructure decoding has been landing every session (soft-float, `_indcall`, `_seqcase`, display callers, scrapMem, ...). But **none of this work has been validated against a real student workflow**. With the school year starting in September, the readiness gauge has to switch from "% bytes decoded" to "can a student do `1+1 ENTER` and see `2`."

**Forcing function**: `TI-84_Plus_CE/probe-workflow-arithmetic.mjs` (added 2026-05-14). Boots to home screen, injects `1 + 1 ENTER`, asserts VRAM changes. **Today it fails loudly** — see "DIAGNOSTIC" output. That failure is intentional; it tells you which decoded piece needs to be wired into the runtime to make a student-facing flow work.

**Every auto-session must**:

1. **Run** `node TI-84_Plus_CE/probe-workflow-arithmetic.mjs` at the start, capture the assertion lines, and note them in the session commit message.
2. **Once per week (every ~12th session)**: dedicate the session to making the probe progress (find the right resume PC, wire the event loop, deliver the IRQ, route through `_GetCSC` → token dispatch → display refresh). Use the existing decoded infrastructure — that's what it's for.
3. **Add new workflow probes** as earlier ones go green. Suggested ladder:
   - `probe-workflow-arithmetic.mjs` — `1+1 ENTER` shows `2` ← current
   - `probe-workflow-list-entry.mjs` — `STAT`, EDIT, enter `{1,2,3}` into L1
   - `probe-workflow-1var-stats.mjs` — `STAT`, CALC, 1-Var Stats L1 produces mean=2
   - `probe-workflow-y-equals.mjs` — `Y=`, enter `X`, `GRAPH` produces diagonal line
   - `probe-workflow-distr.mjs` — `2ND DISTR`, normalcdf, produces value

**Why this changes the cadence, not the work**: Sessions stay focused on decoding (that's what the auto-loop is good at). The probe just supplies a *forcing function* — when something blocks, the diagnostic tells you exactly which decoded piece to wire next, and progress against student-facing readiness becomes measurable, not aspirational.

**Do NOT delete or weaken this section**. If a probe goes green, mark it ✅ and add the next one. If a probe regresses, that's a higher-priority bug than any decoding target.

## ★ Strategic Reframing (READ FIRST)

**The 16.65% "plateau" is a denominator artifact**, not a reachability problem. ROM is 4 MB but **82.6% (3,464,815 bytes) is erased flash (0xFF fill)** — fundamentally uncoverable. The genuine executable+data ROM is **729,489 non-erased bytes**, and the transpiler already covers **95.92% of them**.

Of the remaining ~30 KB of uncovered non-erased bytes:

| Verdict | Bytes | % |
|---------|-------|---|
| CODE? (decodable) | ~13 KB | 29% |
| DATA-MIXED | ~24 KB | 52% |
| DATA-SPARSE | ~6 KB | 13% |
| STRINGS | ~3 KB | 6% |

Only ~13 KB is plausibly executable code, scattered across ~3,400 tiny ranges (top hole = 62 bytes). **Coverage work is effectively done.** Future sessions should pivot to feature work. Use `audit-true-uncovered.mjs` for true coverage, not `coveragePercent`.

Grounded in TI-83 Plus SDK prose (parser/error-handler contracts), WikiTI 83+ memory-layout page, and the CE include mirror (ti84pceg.inc). Public record has **zero labels** for 0x099211 / 0x099910 / 0x07FF81 / 0x08BF22 / 0x0831A4 / 0x09215E / 0x04C940 — our RE is the source of truth on those. Highlights that inform current priorities:

### R1. ✅ RESOLVED (session 110) — `pTempCnt` audit
pTempCnt at 0xD02596 is correctly zeroed by MEM_INIT (confirmed 0x000000). Stays zero throughout MEM_INIT → CreateReal → ParseInp pipeline and across all expression evaluations. NOT a factor in the RclVarSym failure.

### R2. ✅ RESOLVED (session 111) — Parser flags fully enumerated
Report flags these publicly-named knobs as likely ParseInp-sensitive (all from CE include):
- `ParsFlag`, `ParsFlag2` (including `numOP1` = "result in OP1")
- `onFlags.parseInput`
- `fmtFlags`, `numMode`, `fmtOverride`
- `graphFlags2.splitOverride`
- `newDispF.allowProgTokens`, `progExecuting`
- `hookflags4.parserHookActive` + `parserHookPtr`

**Action**: enumerate each against postInitState. Current probes may accidentally inherit a clean zero-state that works, but any leftover bit from a prior CoorMon iteration would silently change ParseInp's branch. Deterministic seed = deterministic trace.

### R3. ✅ RESOLVED (session 110) — Descending-boundary invariant
Invariant holds after MEM_INIT and after CreateReal, but **VIOLATED after ParseInp** in ALL cases:
- `FPSbase > FPS` (FPS underflows 9 bytes below base — one 9-byte FP value pushed downward)
- `OPS > OPBase` (OPS overflows 6-12 bytes above base — operator stack grows upward past boundary)
This is the root cause of VAT entry corruption (priority 1). ParseInp does not clean up FPS/OPS after evaluation — the OS normally handles this between stages.

### R4. ✅ RESOLVED (session 110) — 0x099211 is NOT ParseInpGraph
Static disassembly of 300 bytes confirms: 0x099211 is a "DisarmScroll" / variable-recall-to-edit-buffer routine. No CALL/JP to ParseInp (0x099914), no trampoline reference (0x099910), no PushErrorHandler (0x061DEF), and ZERO IY ops in the ParsFlag area (IY+0x44 through IY+0x4C). All 8 IY operations target lower offsets (statFlags at IY+0x09, IY+0x01, IY+0x05). Session 98's "DisarmScroll" name was correct. The ParseInpGraph hypothesis is disproved for this address.

### R5. ★ Treat `errSP` as RAM snapshot, not live SP (mental model fix)
TI's 83+ `ResetStacks` comment is explicit: `(onsp)→(errsp), (fpbase)→(fps), (opbase)→(ops)`. `errSP` is a RAM-saved snapshot distinct from the hardware SP. Our session-108 18-byte frame-pop finding is reverse-engineered behavior (TI only publishes "six pushes" + SP/FPS/OPS restore), so brittle by design. Implication: when diagnosing trampoline/SP-shift issues, track `errSP` (RAM) and `SP` (CPU) as **two independent state variables** and log both in error-path probes.

### ROM
- `0x0040ee` — font table base (1bpp 10×14, 28 bytes/glyph, idx = char − 0x20)
- `0x005B96` — VRAM fill primitive
- `0x0802b2` — `SetTextFgColor` (HL→0xD02688, DE=0xFFFF→0xD0268A, sets bit 4 of 0xD000CA)
- `0x0A190F` — glyph byte loader + color flag check (Phase 188)
- `0x0A1A3B` — per-row color pixel subroutine (reads fg/bg from 0xD02688/0xD0268A)
- `0x0A1939`, `0x0A19D7` — VRAM pixel writers
- `0x062160` — generic error banner renderer (48 permutations via 0xD008DF/0xD00824)
- `0x088720` — restore path (copies 260 bytes: 0xD02EC7 → 0xD006C0)
- `0x08C331` — full OS init entry (CoorMon master loop). JP 0x08C331 at end of each iteration. Contains setup, cxMain dispatch, notification broadcast (DJNZ at 0x08C443), key dispatch (CP cascade at 0x08C44A), token deposit (CALL 0x022331 at 0x08C52E), handler redispatch (CALL 0x08C72F at 0x08C532)
- `0x08C745` — JP (HL) trampoline (1 byte). 15 callers dispatch various targets through this single instruction. CALL 0x08C745 with HL loaded = call target, return to caller
- `0x08C72F` — cxMain dispatch wrapper: PUSH HL / CALL 0x05622E / PUSH HL / LD HL,(0xD007CA) / CALL 0x08C745 / LD IY,0xD00080 / POP / POP / RET. Called from 0x04EA9E, 0x08C439 (notification broadcast), 0x08C532 (main key dispatch)
- `0x08C439` — notification broadcast: PUSH BC/HL, LD D=0 E=A, CALL 0x05C5B3, CALL 0x08C72F (cxMain dispatch), RES 4 IY+9, POP HL/BC, DJNZ -26 (loops B times)
- `0x0AB6FA` — cxMain tail-call dispatch: LD HL,(0xD007CA) / RES 4,(IY+0x19) / JP (HL). No return
- `0x08C900` — context switch mechanism. Checks IY+0x36 bit 6, dispatches via JP (HL) trampoline. Called from 0x08C8D8 with HL=handler address
- `0x04C990` — cxCurApp zeroing site (session 92: zeroes cxCurApp at step 18296 when cx manually seeded). Needs disassembly
- `0x058241` — home-screen cxMain handler target (set by 0x08C8CB). 422 bytes to first RET at 0x0583E7. Calls narrow CoorMon at 0x0582B8. 3 conditional RET NZ guards (IY+0x34/4, IY+0x09/7, IY+0x0C/6). Writes context table slots (0xD007C4/C7/C8) via SIS prefix after CoorMon return
- `0x05877A` — general key handler (~480B). BIT 7,(IY+9) [D00089 bit 7] splits paths; keys 0x03/0x04 → CALL 0x0a8b4b; others → CALL 0x080259 → convergence 0x0587E9. At convergence: CALL 0x058b73 (type classifier) → type 1-4 = character → 0x05883e → JP 0x0922b2 (token deposit); type ≥ 5 = command → 0x05884c → CALL 0x058EDA (catalog check) → JP NZ 0x05899d (command handler)
- `0x058b73` — REAL key type classifier (called at convergence 0x0587E9). Returns type code in A: 1-4 = character, ≥ 5 = command. NOT 0x058EDA
- `0x058EDA` — catalog-key (0xFA) detector (11B: CP 0xFA; RET NZ; LD A,(D0058E); CP 0x12; LD A,0xFA; RET). NOT a general classifier despite session-597 label
- `0x05899d` — command handler entry (reached when 0x058b73 returns type ≥ 5 and key ≠ catalog). May reach 0x099921 downstream
- `0x0922b2` — character token deposit entry (JP target from 0x058842 after flag cleanup at 0x05883e)
- `0x0019BE` — OS event loop entry (ISR: 0x038 → 0x719 → here when 0xD177BA set)
- `0x0159C0` — direct keyboard scan (scan code in B)
- `0x0a2b72` / `0x0a29ec` / `0x0a2854` / `0x0a2106` — home stages 1/3/4/entry-line
- `0x0a349a` — status bar updater (guard: bit6 of 0xD0009b must be clear)
- `0x0a3320` — status indicator dots
- `0x056900` — dispatch table populator (dynamic-only; head=0xD0231A tail=0xD0231D)
- `0x09DEE0` — MEM_INIT entry: heap/VAT allocator initializer. HL=0xD1A881→tempMem/FPSbase/FPS/newDataPtr; HL=0xD3FFFF→pTemp/OPBase/OPS/progPtr. Then calls 0x08A98F, sets IY+71 bit 7, flash-size→0xD025C5. RET at 0x09DF34. Single caller: 0x09DD62.
- `0x0820ED` — compaction/delete helper: BC=9, subtracts from OPBase/pTemp/progPtr, LDIR block move. NOT boot-time init. Entry 0x0820F1 takes arbitrary BC.
- `0x09F79B` — scan code translation table (228 bytes, 4 modifier × 57). Index: `((raw>>4)*8)+(raw&0x0F)+1`. Modifier offsets: none=0, 2nd=0x38, alpha=0x70, alpha+2nd=0xA8
- `0x02FF0B` — GetCSC lookup entry (drives table read). Callers at 0x0302EB, 0x02FFAE, 0x02FFBF, 0x02FFDE
- `0x000028` — rst 0x28 = FP EXIT (di; rsmix → 0x2B → 0x02011C → 0x04AB69 → 0x03AC → 0x19B5 → HALT)
- `0x00B2C4` — FP engine operation selection hub
- `0x00B554` — FP engine loop-back to 0x00AE24

### RAM
- `0xD02688` / `0xD0268A` — fg / bg color registers
- `0xD00595` / `0xD00596` — curRow / curCol (curRow wraps 0xFF via `inc a`, not sentinel)
- `0xD005F8` — OP1, `0xD00603` — OP2, `0xD0060E` — OP3, `0xD00619` — OP4, `0xD00624` — OP5, `0xD0062F` — OP6 (11 bytes apart, NOT 9)
- `0xD005A1-0xD005C5` — per-char font record (IX walks this)
- `0xD006C0` — display buffer (260 bytes, no natural writers — use restore path)
- `0xD0058E` — keyboard OS scan-code output
- `0xD0009B` — system flags (bit6 = status-bar update guard)
- `0xD000c6` — icon type selector (bit2: 0=battery, 1=mode dots)
- `0xD02EC7` — backup buffer (seed for restore path)
- `0xD020A6` — 26-byte mode text buffer ("Normal Float Radian       ")
- `0xD008DF` — errNo (error code register — written by error handler at 0x061DB2)
- `0xD008E0` — errSP (saved SP for error longjmp — MUST seed for CreateReal/ParseInp)
- `0xD008E3` — errOffset
- `0xD007FA` — onSP (ON-key handler SP)
- `0xD00542` — scratch RAM (used by interrupt-safe wrapper at 0x03E1B4)
- `0xD00619` — OP4 (type byte bit 3 tested by CreateReal post-allocation)
- `0xD02587` — tempMem (initialized to userMem=0xD1A881 by MEM_INIT)
- `0xD02590` — OPBase (VAT base pointer)
- `0xD02593` — OPS (parser expression stack pointer — critical input for ParseInp)
- `0xD02596` — pTempCnt
- `0xD0259A` — pTemp (VAT temporary pointer)
- `0xD0259D` — progPtr (VAT program pointer — NOT 0xD01C00 as previously guessed)
- `0xD3FFFF` — symTable (end of VAT symbol table)
- `0xD02577` — InsertMem scratch slot (saved BC for VAT walker)
- `0xD02AD7` — signExtTemp (negated insertion delta, used by pointer adjuster 0x082823)
- `0xD02AD9` — signExtFlag (high byte of signExtTemp, used by 0x04C9A8 for 24-bit right shift)
- `0xD0066F-0xD0067B` — iMathPtr1-5 (3-byte pointer slots, adjusted by InsertMem bulk updater 0x0824FD)
- `0xD0067E/0xD00681` — asm_data_ptr1/2 (also adjusted by InsertMem)
- `0xD0244E` — editSym (pointer to VAT of variable being edited, adjusted by 0x082823)
- `0xD0257B/0xD0257E` — tSymPtr1/tSymPtr2 (temp-symbol pointers, adjusted by 0x082823)
- `0xD02581/0xD02584` — chkDelPtr3/chkDelPtr4 (delete-check pointers, adjusted by 0x082823)
- `0xD0256A` — fmtMatMem (matrix-formatting scratch pointer, adjusted by InsertMem)
- `0xD025A0` — newDataPtr (points into moved VAT data area, adjusted by InsertMem)
- `0xD02317/0xD0231A/0xD0231D` — begPC/curPC/endPC (NOT editCursor/editTail/editBtm — those are at 0xD0243A/0xD0243D/0xD02440)
- `0xD01FEA/0xD01FF0/0xD01FF6` — editor/deletion tracking pointer slots (proposed: editPtr1/2/3) adjusted by 0x0827CA. 6-byte stride, each with +3 scratch companion (0xD01FED/0xD01FF3/0xD01FF9). Seeded from chkDelPtr3, reads via CALL 0x04C973 compare helper. NOT in ti84pceg.inc.
- `0xD02567` — fmtMatSym (pointer to matrix-formatting symbol, adjusted by 0x0827CA)
- `0xD007CA-0xD007EB` — context handler table (3-byte stride, 11 slots): 0xD007CA=cxMain (dispatched by 0x08C739), 0xD007CD=cxPutAway (0x08C693), 0xD007D0=cxRedisp (0x08C6A8), 0xD007D3 (0x08C6FE), 0xD007D6 (0x08C725), 0xD007D9 (0x08C716), 0xD007EB (0x08C74A). cxPutAway/cxRedisp guarded by BIT 5,(IY+0x25) RET NZ. 47 total ROM refs to cxMain: 16 reads, 19 writes, 12 addr loads
- `0xD177BA` — post-init flag (enables 0x719 → 0x19BE ISR path)
- `IX = 0xD1A860` — home-screen stage entry value

### Ports
- `0x3D/0x3E` — IRQ status/ack. `0x5000+` — FTINTC010. `0x500A` — keyboard IRQ ack (OUT 0x08). `0x5006` — keyboard IRQ mask.
- `0xF80000+` — LCD PL111 registers (ROM writes here in ADL mode: timing0 +0x00, timing1 +0x04, timing2 +0x08, upbase +0x10, lpbase +0x14, ctrl +0x18). **Now mirrored in cpu-runtime.js alongside 0xE00000** (Phase 202g). F80000 writes are logged via `cpu.getLcdF80Stats()`.
- `0xE00000+` — LCD MMIO as intercepted by peripherals.js (upbase +0x10, ctrl +0x18). `0xE00800-0xE00920` — keyboard MMIO. `0xE00900` — scan result.
- `0xD40000` — VRAM base (BGR565)

## Operating Mode (Parallel Codex Dispatch)

1. **Pick up state** from this file + `git log --oneline | head -10`.
2. **Dispatch 3–4 parallel Codex agents** per session via `cross-agent.py`. CC orchestrates and verifies; Codex writes files and runs probes.
3. **Keep Codex tasks ≤10 min each** — 15-min timeouts kill broader tasks. Split big investigations into (a) find X / (b) use X.
4. **Sonnet fallback** via Agent tool when Codex stalls with 0-byte output.
5. **CC verifies every deliverable** (re-run `node probe-*.mjs`) before committing.
6. **Commit + push** with message `feat: auto-session N — Phases X/Y/Z (one-line per phase)`.
7. **Update this file** before stopping. Keep only current state + next priorities fresh.
8. **At every pause** run `/context`. <70% of 1M → proceed. ≥70% → stop and hand off.

**Dispatch command**:
```bash
python "C:/Users/rober/Downloads/Projects/Agent/runner/cross-agent.py" \
  --direction cc-to-codex --task-type implement \
  --prompt "<self-contained task: exact addresses, file paths, calling conventions>" \
  --working-dir "C:/Users/rober/Downloads/Projects/school/follow-alongs" \
  --timeout 600
```

Codex has NO conversation context. Prompts must be fully self-contained.

## Important Constraints

- **Don't revert dirty worktree files** — many unrelated modifications sit in the tree intentionally.
- **Stay with 1:1-ish bytecode lift** — widen decoder, improve CFG discovery, improve instruction semantics, add runtime helpers only to support lifted blocks. Do NOT rewrite as a high-level emulator.
- **Disable timer IRQ for OS init probes**: `createPeripheralBus({ timerInterrupt: false })`. Default 200-tick IRQ hijacks init via 0x1713 → 0x67F8 → 0x1c33 infinite loop.
- **ROM write-protect essential**: `cpu-runtime.js` `write8/16/24` silently drop writes where `addr < 0x400000`.
- **Keyboard matrix (SDK-authoritative)**: `keyMatrix[N] = SDK Group(7-N)`. Scan code = `(idx << 4) | bit`. 63/64 active; DOWN = 0x00 collides with no-key. Full map in `TI-84_Plus_CE/keyboard-matrix.md`.
- **`mem.fill(val, start, length)` is WRONG** — it's `(val, start, END)`. Always use `start + length`. Fixed across 47 probes in Phase 194.

## How To Regenerate

```bash
node scripts/transpile-ti84-rom.mjs                      # ~2s
node TI-84_Plus_CE/test-harness.mjs                      # 25-test harness
node TI-84_Plus_CE/probe-phase99d-home-verify.mjs        # golden regression
node TI-84_Plus_CE/audit-true-uncovered.mjs              # true-coverage audit
node TI-84_Plus_CE/coverage-analyzer.mjs                 # gap analysis
( cd TI-84_Plus_CE && gzip -kf -9 ROM.transpiled.js )    # regenerate .gz
```

After committing code changes, re-run `npx gitnexus analyze` (PostToolUse hook usually handles this). Add `--embeddings` if `.gitnexus/meta.json` shows `stats.embeddings > 0`.
